note: The measured layer holds fifteen figure rows and no table row at all: all seven printed tables are typeset with live text and, in every case checked, no drawn rule, no fill and no banding, so the region pass had nothing to measure. The newspaper sheet p25 is one full-page 1440x2080 raster and the pass boxed only the team stamp on it. Both deficits are recorded rather than papered over.
rules: Seven tables print and not one owns a measured region: Tables 1-7 are set in live text with no drawn rule, no fill and no banding, and the p4, p8, p11, p18 and p20 bands carry exactly zero drawing operators, so both the rule detector and the vector-cluster pass return nothing there. The census therefore holds fifteen figure rows and no table-grid row at all, so [geometry.family] never takes the value table-grid anywhere in this paper and the deficit between printed exhibits and recorded exhibits is seven.

The newspaper sheet p25 is a single full-page 1440x2080 raster - one banner photo, three inset photos and every word of the article inside one image - and the pass boxed only the team stamp in its corner. That content was never measured, so it cannot be a row: it is a declared deficit, not an exclusion, and [geometry.family] is never recorded for it.

Figure numbers print twice or three times: "Figure 2" captions the biomass curve on p6 and the NDVI raster on p7, "Figure 12" captions the tree cover chart on p20 and the Kuznets curve on p21, and "Figure 14" is announced on p22 and captioned on p23. [caption.verbatim] keeps the printed number on each row, so fifteen exhibits carry eleven distinct numbers - the count a "Figures per paper" statistic would get wrong.

Two numbers are cited and never printed: "Figure 3" on p9 and "Figure 15" on p23, the second wrapped across a line break, and the same page also points at "Figure x" with no number at all. [mention.count] stays 0 on the rows they would otherwise be attached to and no row is invented for them.

Four captions lose their mathematical symbol in the text layer, so four rows are typed from the crop: Figure 13 prints "Figure 13. Forest's δ−TGTG Curve" while the layer doubles every glyph, Figure 14 ends at "Sensitivity analysis of" with the symbol gone, and Figures 6 and 8 print "COI" where the layer holds six mathematical C glyphs. [caption.verbatim] is what the page shows, not what the layer holds.

Captions are reused verbatim: Figure 12 on p20 carries Figure 9's caption word for word, and the same seam runs through the tables the census could not measure - Table 2 repeats Table 1's "Notations used in this paper" over a species growth-rate grid, and Tables 5 and 6 share one caption on p14 and p18 while printing different grids. [caption.verbatim] records the duplication rather than silently repairing it.

Caption side is unanimous and independent of the box edge: all fifteen figure captions print BELOW their art, and four of them - Figures 6, 8, 13 and 14 - print INSIDE the bottom of their bounding box, 1.6 to 17.3 pt above the measured edge. [caption.position] is therefore read against the region midpoint, not against y1, or those four would flip to "above".

Five exhibits print above the heading of the section that follows them and the context pass attached every one to the wrong section: Figure 6 prints over 5.2 Economic benefit model, Figure 11 over 6.3, Figure 13 over section 7 and Figure 14 over section 8, while Figure 7 prints on p16 beneath the section 6 heading. [place.section_path] is overridden on ten rows against the printed heading order, which is the only authority that survives a page-opening exhibit.

Every pointer is ASCII and numbered - "Figure N" and "Table N", no "Fig.", no ligature - so the ligature hazard that hides pointers elsewhere in this block does not bite here; the single wrapped pointer ("Figure" at the foot of a line, "15" at the head of the next) is the only one a line-scoped scan misses. [mention.style] keeps each printed spelling.

Eight of the fifteen rows carry no pointer at all - Figures 1, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 13 and the second "Figure 12" - while Figure 4 is pointed at one page AFTER it prints ("as shown in the Figure 4" on p10 for a chart on p9), so [mention.count] runs the whole range from 0 to 1 and the four page-level leads are not all in the same direction.

Only two of the seven cited exhibits are read back numerically in the body - Figure 8 returns its 35.69 and Figure 14 returns "3.5 percent at a rate of 0.05" - and the rest are introduced and never quoted. [mention.read_sentences] is 1 on those two rows and 0 on the other thirteen.
